title: सुदूरपश्चिम प्रदेशको भाषिक स्थिति Sudurpaschim Pradeshko Bhashik Sthiti
authors: बम Bam, सुरेन्द्र Surendra कुमार Kumar
nepali: सुदूरपश्चिम प्रदेशकोको भाषिक स्थितिमा केन्द्रित यस लेखको मुख्य उद्दश्ेय सुदूरपश्चिम प्रदेशको भाषिक अवस्था पहिचान गर्नु रहेको छ । प्रादेशिक संरचना नेपालको नयाँ व्यवस्था भएकाले प्रदेशगत रूपमा भाषिक तथ्याङ्क पर्याप्त रूपमा उपलब्ध छैन । प्रस्तुत लेखमा शीर्षकसँग सम्बन्धित सैद्धान्तिक सामग्रीको अध्ययन गरी प्राप्त तथ्यको मिश्रित ढाँचामा व्याख्या विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । २०६८ सालको जनगणना अनुसार सुदूरपश्चिम प्रदेशमा बोलिने ८३ ओटा भाषा मध्ये नेपालीका अतिरिक्त एक दर्जन भाषाको मूल उत्पत्ति र प्रमुख प्रयोग क्षेत्र यसै प्रदेशमा भएका रैथाने भाषा रहेको पाइएको छ । वक्ता सङ्ख्याका आधारमा डोटेली सबैभन्दा ठूलो भाषा रहेको यस प्रदेशमा नेपाली दोस्रो, थारु तेस्रो, बैतडेली चौथो र अछामी पाँचौं स्थानमा रहेका छन् । नेपालमा बोलिने चारै परिवारका भाषा बोलिने यस प्रदेशमा ९८ प्रतिशतभन्दा बढीले भारोपेली परिवारका भाषा बोल्ने गरेको पाइन्छ । अधिकांश भाषा कथ्य रूपमा रहेको यस प्रदेशमा नेपालीका अतिरिक्त डोटेली र थारु भाषाको मात्र अलि बढी लेख्य परम्परा रहेको छ भने अरु केही भाषाको लेख्य परम्परा भर्खर सुरु भएको पाइन्छ । परम्परागत ज्ञानको खानी र इतिहासको धरोहरका रूपमा रहेका प्रदेशका समग्र भाषाहरूको संरक्षण, सम्बर्धन र विकासका लागि सम्बन्धित सबैको ध्यान जानु आवश्यक देखिन्छ ।
american_english: The main objective of this article, which is focused on the linguistic situation of Sudurpashchim Province, is to identify the linguistic condition of Sudurpashchim Province. Since the provincial structure is a new arrangement in Nepal, linguistic statistics are not sufficiently available on a province-by-province basis. In the present article, theoretical material related to the topic has been studied and the facts obtained have been explained and analyzed in a mixed format. According to the 2068 BS census, among the 83 languages spoken in Sudurpashchim Province, apart from Nepali, a dozen languages were found to be indigenous languages whose original origin and main area of use are in this very province. On the basis of the number of speakers, Doteli is the largest language in this province, while Nepali is in second place, Tharu in third, Baitadeli in fourth, and Achhami in fifth. In this province, where languages of all four families spoken in Nepal are spoken, it is found that more than 98 percent speak languages of the Indo-Aryan family. In this province, where most languages exist in spoken form, apart from Nepali, only the Doteli and Tharu languages have a somewhat greater written tradition, while it is found that the written tradition of some other languages has only recently begun. It appears necessary for the attention of all concerned to go toward the preservation, promotion, and development of all the languages of the province, which remain as a storehouse of traditional knowledge and as a heritage of history.

informal_english: The main goal of this article, which zeroes in on the language situation in Sudurpashchim Province, is to figure out what the linguistic condition of Sudurpashchim Province looks like. Since the provincial setup is a new thing in Nepal, language stats aren't really available in enough detail on a province-by-province basis. In this article, theoretical material related to the topic has been studied, and the facts gathered have been explained and analyzed in a mixed format. According to the 2068 BS census, out of the 83 languages spoken in Sudurpashchim Province, besides Nepali, a dozen languages turned out to be indigenous languages whose original roots and main area of use are right here in this province. Based on the number of speakers, Doteli is the biggest language in this province, while Nepali comes in second, Tharu third, Baitadeli fourth, and Achhami fifth. In this province, where languages from all four families spoken in Nepal are spoken, it turns out that more than 98 percent of people speak languages from the Indo-Aryan family. In this province, where most languages are mainly spoken, besides Nepali, only Doteli and Tharu have a somewhat stronger written tradition, while it looks like the written tradition of some other languages has only just gotten started. It seems like everyone concerned needs to pay attention to preserving, promoting, and developing all the languages of the province, which stand as a treasure trove of traditional knowledge and a heritage of history.
